A shop's server asks Tegata for a **checkout session**, sends the customer to its page, and gets a signed
**webhook** when the payment has settled on NEAR. The business receives exactly the amount, in USDC on NEAR.

<Steps>
<Step>

**Make a key.** In the app, open **Developers** and press **New key**. The key is shown once; Tegata keeps only its
SHA-256 hash and shows its first characters after that. Sandbox keys start `tk_test_` and work on NEAR testnet.

</Step>
<Step>

**Add an endpoint.** Type your https URL and press **Add endpoint**, or press **Use Tegata's test inbox** to see
webhooks arrive without a server of your own. Each endpoint gets its own signing secret (`whsec_…`), shown once and
behind **Reveal secret** after that.

</Step>
<Step>

**Create a session** with the curl below, and send your customer to its `url`.

</Step>
<Step>

**Fulfil the order** when `checkout.session.completed` arrives.

</Step>
</Steps>

<Shot src="/shots/wide/app-developers.webp" alt="The Developers page: the checkout session curl, an API key named Shop server, Tegata's test inbox as a webhook endpoint with Send test event, Reveal secret and Remove, and the test inbox list" caption="The Developers page: the quickstart, your keys, your endpoints and the test inbox." address="tegata.xyz/app/developers" />

## Create a checkout session

```bash
curl https://tegata.xyz/api/v1/checkout/sessions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEGATA_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: order-1042" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"amount": "25.00", "description": "Order #1042",
       "success_url": "https://your-shop.example/thanks",
       "metadata": {"order": "1042"}}'
```

| Field | What it takes |
| --- | --- |
| `amount` | Dollars, as `"25"`, `"25.50"` or `25.5`. From 0.01 to 1,000,000 |
| `description` | What the payer sees on the page and the receipt, up to 80 characters. Optional |
| `success_url` | An https address. Once paid, the page shows **Back to** your business, linking there. Optional |
| `metadata` | Up to 20 keys, each value a string of up to 500 characters. Comes back on the session and in its webhooks. Optional |

Send an **`Idempotency-Key`** header (up to 200 characters) and a retry with the same key returns the same session
instead of a second one. The reply is `201` with the session.

A session is paid once, in full: the page takes no part-payments, and it is open until it's paid.

## The session

This is the real session from the proof run below, read back after it was paid (it ran against the app on
`localhost`, on NEAR testnet):

```json
{
  "id": "2f852836-9206-492e-9d6e-830148366c96",
  "object": "checkout.session",
  "status": "complete",
  "url": "http://localhost:3100/pay/E32DvMBiifrjmx",
  "amount": "0.25",
  "amount_units": "250000",
  "currency": "usd",
  "settlement": { "asset": "USDC", "network": "near-testnet", "account": "dev-eee78deb.tegata.testnet" },
  "description": "Order #1042",
  "success_url": "https://shop.example/thanks",
  "metadata": { "order": "1042" },
  "payment": {
    "id": "35fc8d8f-dabe-4c8f-9302-d37e1389b34c",
    "object": "payment",
    "amount": "0.25",
    "amount_units": "250000",
    "refunded_units": "0",
    "currency": "usd",
    "rail": "near_wallet",
    "payer": "customer-eab2310f.tegata.testnet",
    "network": "near-testnet",
    "tx_hash": "6tmnGKULQVyUUeGdpWNQYLNWCrCCmiv4iqQtsimSnBnF",
    "request_id": "2f852836-9206-492e-9d6e-830148366c96",
    "settled_at": "2026-11-13T07:23:50.807Z"
  },
  "created_at": "2026-11-13T07:23:30.520Z"
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `status` | `open` until paid, then `complete` |
| `amount_units` | The same amount in USDC base units (6 decimals) |
| `settlement` | Where the money lands: USDC, the NEAR network, the business's account |
| `payment` | `null` until paid; then who paid, how (`tegata` for a Tegata balance, `near_wallet`), and the NEAR transaction |

## Read it back

```bash
curl https://tegata.xyz/api/v1/checkout/sessions/<id> \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEGATA_KEY"
```

`GET /api/v1/events?limit=20` lists the latest events, newest first (up to 100), with the same bodies webhooks carry.

Errors come back as `{"error": {"code": "…", "message": "…"}}`:

| Status | When |
| --- | --- |
| `401` | No key, a wrong key, or a revoked one |
| `400` | A field that doesn't fit, such as an amount out of range or a `success_url` that isn't https |
| `404` | A session that isn't yours |

## Webhooks

| Event | Sent when |
| --- | --- |
| `checkout.session.completed` | A session is paid in full |
| `payment.succeeded` | Any payment to the business settles: a session, a pay link, an invoice, a counter sale |
| `payment.refunded` | The business refunds a payment, all or part |
| `invoice.paid` | An invoice is paid in full |

Each event is stored once and sent to every endpoint that's switched on. The body:

```json
{
  "id": "838bc31c-f2d2-455a-908a-cd6e84caa6f0",
  "type": "checkout.session.completed",
  "created_at": "2026-11-13T07:23:50.806Z",
  "data": { "id": "2f852836-…", "object": "checkout.session", "status": "complete", "amount": "0.25",
            "metadata": { "order": "1042" }, "payment": { "tx_hash": "6tmnGKULQVyUUeGdpWNQYLNWCrCCmiv4iqQtsimSnBnF", "…": "…" } }
}
```

It is signed with [Standard Webhooks](https://www.standardwebhooks.com): the headers `webhook-id`,
`webhook-timestamp` and `webhook-signature`, an HMAC with your endpoint's secret. Check it with the
`standardwebhooks` library before you trust a body:

```js
import { Webhook } from "standardwebhooks"

const wh = new Webhook(process.env.TEGATA_WEBHOOK_SECRET) // whsec_…
// In your handler, with the raw body as a string:
const event = wh.verify(rawBody, {
  "webhook-id": req.headers["webhook-id"],
  "webhook-timestamp": req.headers["webhook-timestamp"],
  "webhook-signature": req.headers["webhook-signature"],
})
if (event.type === "checkout.session.completed") fulfil(event.data.metadata.order)
```

`webhook-id` stays the same across retries of one delivery, so use it to ignore a repeat.

| Rule | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Success | Any 2xx within 10 seconds. Redirects are not followed |
| Retries | After 30 s, 2 min, 10 min, 1 h and 6 h: six tries in all, then the delivery is marked failed |
| Endpoints | https only, and never an address inside a private network. Up to 5 per business |
| **Send test event** | A `ping` event to that endpoint only, now |
| **Resend** | Any delivery in the log, again |

The **Deliveries** log shows each event, the endpoint, the last status code and the number of tries.

## The test inbox

**Use Tegata's test inbox** adds an endpoint that Tegata hosts. It records every webhook that arrives and checks its
signature, so the **Test inbox** list shows each event with "Signature valid" or "Bad signature". It is the quickest
way to watch the whole loop before writing a handler.

## A pay button

For a fixed price with no server, point a button at a [pay link](/docs/guide/pay-links):

```html
<a href="https://tegata.xyz/pay/YOUR_LINK_TOKEN"
   style="display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;padding:12px 20px;border-radius:14px;
          background:#FF4F00;color:#fff;font:600 16px system-ui;text-decoration:none">
  Pay with Tegata
</a>
```

## A real one

`packages/services/src/proofs/developers.ts` runs the whole loop on NEAR testnet, with the app and the worker
running:

1. A business gets an API key, and Tegata's test inbox as its endpoint.
2. A real `curl` creates the session above. The same `Idempotency-Key` sent again returns the same session.
3. A customer with its own NEAR account pays it the way a NEAR wallet does: <Tx hash="6tmnGKULQVyUUeGdpWNQYLNWCrCCmiv4iqQtsimSnBnF" />.
4. The worker reads the USDC transfer from NEAR, marks the session complete and sends `payment.succeeded` and
   `checkout.session.completed`. Both arrive at the inbox with valid signatures and a `200`.
5. A second `curl` reads the session back as `complete`, with the transaction hash.

The session was created at 07:23:30 and paid at 07:23:50.

<Callout title="Sandbox only, for now">
  API keys are made on the network you're on, and Live is not open yet, so every key today is a `tk_test_` key on
  NEAR testnet. Payers pay with a Tegata balance or a NEAR wallet; paying a session from another chain arrives with
  Live.
</Callout>
